reference: GNU coreutils stat from the isolated /usr tree, invoked by the same Bash script and against the same relative fixture setup. GNU stat is the oracle for CLI output, status, and fixture tree; the Bash-only -A extension and loadable metadata use documented contract expectations.
coverage: Stable GNU format directives for regular and empty files, including mode, type, size, quoting, block size, device fields, alignment, and literal percent.
Directory and symbolic-link lstat reporting, plus -L and --dereference target reporting.
Hard-link count, multiple operands, -- operand termination, and partial failure status when one operand is missing.
--printf backslash escapes and its lack of an implicit trailing newline.
Bash type/help metadata and the documented associative-array -A extension.
exclusions: Raw default and -t output are not byte-compared because their inode and creation-time fields vary between the harness's independently constructed reference and candidate fixture trees; stable format directives are compared directly.

Character and block device directives and the device-specific default layout are deferred: fixed-major/minor nodes require a disposable VM or an independently reviewed metadata mock. No host device is used.
Security-context output and unusual filesystems are not covered.
Birth/change times and default/terse inode-dependent layouts remain outside cross-fixture byte comparison; access/modify timestamps are explicitly fixed and compared.

Only ordinary bounded integer/string precision and printable ASCII quote-selection cases are extended. Fractional epoch timestamp precision, additional printf flags, control-byte quoting, QUOTING_STYLE overrides and exhaustive quoting styles remain unqualified.

cases.purpose: Compare many stable coreutils format directives on a small regular file with a fixed mode, including quoting, widths, device identifiers, and literal percent.
Check the empty-file type boundary and directory classification with explicit deterministic permissions.
cases.script:
umask 077
: > empty
mkdir folder
stat -c '%n|%F|%a' empty folder

cases.purpose: Check that the default operation reports a symlink itself, including its target, type, size, and permissions.
cases.script:
printf 'xy' > target
ln -s target link
stat --format='%n|%F|%s|%a|%A|%N|%h' link

cases.purpose: Compare both documented dereference spellings while reporting the target file metadata through the link name.
cases.script:
printf 'target-data' > target
ln -s target link
stat -L -c 'short:%n|%F|%s|%a' link
stat --dereference --format='long:%n|%F|%s|%a' link

cases.purpose: Check multiple-operand output and the link count for two names sharing one fixture inode.
cases.script:
printf 'z' > first
ln first second
stat -c '%n|%F|%s|%h' first second

cases.purpose: Compare --printf tab, newline, hexadecimal escapes, zero padding, percent handling, and no implicit final newline.
Check that a missing middle operand sets failure status and emits a diagnostic while successful operands before and after it still produce output.
cases.script:
printf 'a' > before
printf 'bb' > after
if stat --format='%n=%s' before missing after; then exit 0; else rc=$?; fi
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Check that -- ends option parsing and permits statting a relative filename beginning with a dash.
Record GNU's status/output behavior for an unavailable security context and an unknown directive, then compare the loadable's command statuses and output without hiding either result.
cases.script:
printf 'x' > data
if context=$(stat --format='%C' data); then context_rc=0; else context_rc=$?; fi
printf 'context=%s|%s\n' "$context_rc" "$context"
if unknown=$(stat --format='%Q' data); then unknown_rc=0; else unknown_rc=$?; fi
printf 'unknown=%s|%s\n' "$unknown_rc" "$unknown"

cases.purpose: Check the Bash builtin type and that Bash help resolves the loadable's documented help entry. This is metadata coverage, not stat operation coverage.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t stat) == builtin ]]
help stat > metadata.txt
printf 'type=builtin\nhelp=available\n'

cases.purpose: Check the documented -A associative-array extension against a fixed relative regular-file fixture and independently known name, type, permissions, size, and empty link target.
cases.script:
umask 027
printf 'abc' > array-data
stat -A info array-data
printf '%s|%s|%s|%s|<%s>\n' "${info[name]}" "${info[type]}" "${info[perms]}" "${info[size]}" "${info[link]}"

cases.purpose: Qualify character/block device fields and the device-specific default layout with fixed metadata.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with safely created, non-host-attached character and block nodes of fixed major/minor numbers, or an independently reviewed stat metadata mock. The current fixture boundary has no device creation or host device access; expected checks should include %t/%T, %Hr/%Lr, -L behavior, and the device default layout.

cases.purpose: An unknown directive prints a question mark and preserves the rest of the output.
Unavailable security labels fail while completing both file records.
cases.script: printf x > data; printf yz > second; stat -c '%s:%C:%n' data second

cases.purpose: Compare normal GNU printf precision on names, size and symbolic mode, preserving all output bytes.
Compare GNU quoted-name formatting for an ordinary filename containing an apostrophe.
Compare fixed independently assigned nanosecond access/modify timestamps in C locale and UTC.
cases.script:
printf x > data
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; os.utime("data", ns=(946684800123456789,978307200987654321))'
stat -c '%x|%X|%y|%Y' data

cases.purpose: Observe ordinary string truncation and integer minimum-digit precision with width, zero and empty values.
cases.script:
printf abc > data
: > empty
chmod 0640 data
stat --printf='n=<%8.3n> A=<%-6.3A> size=<%8.5s> zero=<%08.5s>\n' data
stat --printf='zero=<%.0s> width=<%5.0s> A=<%5.0A>\n' empty

cases.purpose: Observe GNU shell-escape-always quote selection for ordinary literal filename punctuation, without interpreting those bytes as shell code.
cases.script:
names=('has'"'"'quote' 'two'"'"'apostrophes'"'"'here' 'both'"'"'and"quote' 'cash'"'"'$name' 'slash'"'"'\name' 'grave'"'"'`name')
for name in "${names[@]}"; do printf x > "$name"; stat -c "%N" "$name"; done

cases.purpose: GNU apostrophe quote selection applies independently to an ordinary relative symlink name and target; all output bytes remain compared.
